title: Alpharetrovirus — avian leukosis and sarcoma viruses Coverage Audit
h1: Alpharetrovirus — avian leukosis and sarcoma viruses
standfirst: Alpharetrovirus is the avian genus — avian leukosis virus and the sarcoma viruses that carry a transduced oncogene. It is the simplest layout in the family, gag-pol-env with no accessory genes, and the only one of the four retroviral modules whose fourth feature is a captured host kinase rather than a viral regulator.

sections.title: What the module calls
sections.lede: Three structural features on every genome, and a fourth that only the sarcoma viruses carry.

blocks.html: src is the fourth gene of non-defective Rous sarcoma virus, 3′ of env and fully collinear — a single tblastn HSP covers residues 1–526 at 93–100% identity. It was never called in the deposited vocabulary; the literature probe turned it up. It is built from 5 unique sequences with a minimum cluster size of 3 rather than the default 5, and the identity floor is untouched.

sections.title: Where it does not call, and why

blocks.html: SRC is called on a small minority of exemplars and that is correct biology, not a gap: src is present only in non-defective sarcoma viruses. Sweeping all 294 holdings with nine curated Swiss-Prot v-Src queries finds nine carriers scoring 937–1102 bits and nothing above 69 — a clean break, so the carrier set is bounded. SRC therefore does not take copy_num. Its profile is sound independently of its rate: it recalls 5 of 5 of its own collection, and the real caller annotated it on a held-out carrier at the expected position and length.

GAG, POL and ENV carry copy_num on biology, not on their rates: every replication-competent retrovirus encodes gag, pol and env, so a genome without one is defective and is flagged as missing an essential feature. That flag is true rather than false only if the genomes it lands on really lack the gene, so each of the 11 exemplars without an ENV call was searched by tblastn against the full ENV collection (a called genome, 11864.1046, scores 1170 bits over 99% of an envelope protein). 9 of 11 carry no intact env: 2 have one interrupted by stop codons or frameshifts and 7 keep under half of it. The other two carry an intact env the profiles do not call (11946.11 at 1166 bits, 11961.72 at 1108 bits) — a recall gap in the module, not in the genome, and the quality flag on them is wrong.

99.5% of the 1095 deposited features from this module's taxa are bound by a naming rule. The remainder are recorded in UNASSIGNED and DISCARDED: the first is vocabulary no rule reached, the second is records the source itself calls partial or truncated, which the project discards rather than trains on.

sections.title: Vocabulary saturation
sections.lede: How fast each vocabulary stops growing as genomes are added.

blocks.html: The deposited vocabulary keeps growing; the module's does not. At the depth both reach, 32.4 distinct source strings correspond to 4.0 controlled annotations, a 8.1-fold collapse. The module reaches 95% of its final vocabulary after 25 proteins against the source's 167.

Coverage is measured by annotating genomes through the real GTO pipeline — annotate_by_viral_pssm-GTO.pl, then the transcript-edit and splice passes, then viral_genome_quality.pl — not by a reimplementation. Spliced features are included, which the flat feature-table path cannot represent. Exemplars are clustered at 95% nucleotide identity over 90% of length, so one row is one distinct sequence rather than one deposit: this module's 294 genomes reduce to 45 exemplars, and without that step a rate would report how often a sequence was deposited rather than how often the module calls it. Call rates are taken over the 41 of 44 exemplars this module actually claimed; an unrouted genome contributes no features and counting it would understate every rate, and this is the same denominator the evaluation and the copy_num decisions used.

source_note: Measured 27 October 2026 from the shipped module: the Alpharetrovirus block of Viral_PSSM.json, its profiles and collections, and the 27 October coverage annotation over 44 exemplars de-replicated from 294 genomes. Vocabulary figures come from collections/synonyms.tsv, written by the module's own builder from the naming rules, and count deposited features rather than unique sequences.
